newsitem.title: USA: Intel is not a mirror of chip industry.
newsitem.headline: Intel is not a mirror of chip industry.

text.p: Intel Corp's upbeat outlook for the third quarter sent shares of the semiconductor giant soaring on Tuesday as investors looked to capitalize on evidence of a strengthening personal computer market.

But while many semiconductor stocks were involved in the rally to some degree, analysts say Intel, while the largest semiconductor maker, does not mirror the industry because of its unique position as a monopoly seller of microprocessors.
"The situation at Intel is remarkably different than the rest of the industry," said analyst Drew Peck of Cowen & Co.

"Here you have a company that is a virtual monopoly in what is arguably the largest end market in the technology business -- selling microprocessors for PCs. That gives them enviable control over the pricing environment. They can modulate their prices while the rest of the semiconductor industry is reeling from price erosion."
He and others said chip stocks are rallying because of Intel's new forecast sales will rise instead of staying flat.
"There are a lot of different segments of the semiconductor market and their dynamics differ," said Greg Mischou of Alex Brown.
"Intel has a unique, differentiated product and they'll experience different conditions."
Intel shares shot up 5-5/8 to 94-1/4, followed by big gains in many others such as Atmel Corp's, 4-1/8 gain to 28-1/4 and Altera Corp's gain of four to 52-1/8.
Other big gainers were LSI Logic Corp by 1-1/8 to 23-3/8 and S3 Corp by 1-1/4 to 17-1/4.
It is certain that a number of semiconductor makers who sell products to PC makers will benefit from strengthening PC sales as Intel has, said John Lazlo of PaineWebber.
"It is not only very positive for Intel, it is supportive of other semiconductor makers that have a sizable PC exposure like S3 Corp or Atmel Corp Lazlo said.

But commodity chips, such as DRAMs or memory chips, continue to face excess supply and manufacturing capacity in the market, analysts say, a situation that eroded DRAM prices this year to a fraction of year ago prices.
"Intel is immune to price erosion because they control prices," said Dataquest analyst Gary Grandbois.
And markets for power transisters such as those made by Motorola Co and International Rectifier and chips for analog systems are all pretty weak, Grandbois said.
Micron Technology and Texas Instruments are the largest U.S. memory chip makers. In consolidated trading, Micron rose 1/8 to 26-5/8 and Texas Instruments 3/8 to 50-1/2.
